questions.question: A person bought a book at 31% discount on its printed price. If no discount was given, then he would have to pay Rs. 2,480 more. How much did he pay (in Rs.) for the book?
questions.questionHtml: A person bought a book at 31% discount on its printed price. If no discount was given, then he would have to pay Rs. 2,480 more. How much did he pay (in Rs.) for the book?
questions.solution:
Let the printed price of the book be 100p.

After discount the selling price of the book = 100p - 100p × 31% = 69p      ....(1)

According to the question,

69p + 2480 = 100p

⇒ 31p = 2480

⇒ p = 2480/31 ⇒ p = 80

Now, the price that he paid for the book

⇒ 69 × 80 (From 1) = Rs. 5520

questions.question: The marked price of 85 items was equal to the cost price of 153 items. The selling price of 104 items was equal to the marked price of 65 items. Calculate the percentage profit or loss from the sale of each item.
questions.questionHtml: The marked price of 85 items was equal to the cost price of 153 items. The selling price of 104 items was equal to the marked price of 65 items. Calculate the percentage profit or loss from the sale of each item.
questions.solution:
Given

The marked price of 85 items is the cost price of 153 items

The selling price of 104 items equals the marked price of 65 items

Formula used:

Profit percentage = \(\frac{SP-CP}{CP} \)× 100

Calculation

Let the marked price be M, the selling price be S, and the cost price be C.

⇒ MP × 85 = 153 × CP 

⇒ MP/CP = 153 / 85  = 9/5 

⇒  SP × 104 = MP × 65 

⇒ SP/MP = 65 /104 = 5/8 

Solving this we get the ratio = CP : SP : MP = 40:45:72

∴ Profit percentage = \(\frac{45-40}{40}\)× 100 = 12.5% profit

questions.question: The successive discounts 18%, 10% and 15% are equivalent to a single discount of:
questions.questionHtml: The successive discounts 18%, 10% and 15% are equivalent to a single discount of:
questions.solution:
Given:

Discounts are 18%, 10% and 15%

Concept used:

If the first discount is x% and 2nd discount is y% then Successive Discount Formula –

Total discount = ( x + y – xy /100)%

Calculation:

18 + 10 - [(18)(10)]/100

⇒ 28 - 1.8

⇒ 26.2

Now, adding 15% discount,

26.2 + 15 - [(26.2)(15)/100]

⇒ 41.2 - 3.93

⇒ 37.27

∴ Required answer is 37.27%

 Alternate MethodCalculation:

  M.P S.P
1st discount (- 18%) 50 41
2nd discount (- 10%) 10 9
3rd discount (- 15%) 20 17
Overall discount 10000 6273

Now,

Discount % = (3727/10000) × 100 = 37.27%

∴ The correct answer is 37.27%.

questions.question: The selling price of an article marked for Rs. 10000 after giving three discounts, 20%, 10% and k% is Rs. 6120. What will be selling price (in Rs.) of the same article if a single discount of (k + 20)% is allowed?
questions.questionHtml: The selling price of an article marked for Rs. 10000 after giving three discounts, 20%, 10% and k% is Rs. 6120. What will be selling price (in Rs.) of the same article if a single discount of (k + 20)% is allowed?
questions.solution:
Given:

Marked Price = Rs. 10,000

Three discounts = 20%, 10% and k%

Selling Price = Rs. 6120

Formula used:

SP = MP × [(100 - Discount%)/100]

Calculation:

SP after 1st discount = Rs. 10,000 × [80/100]

⇒ Rs. 8,000

SP after 2nd discount = Rs. 8,000 × [90/100]

⇒ Rs. 7,200

Final discount = Rs. (7,200 – 6,120)

⇒ Rs. 1,080

Discount% = Rs. (1,080/7,200) × 100

⇒ 15%

Single discount of (K + 20) = (15 + 20)%

⇒ 35%

Now, SP after 35% discount = Rs. (10,000 × 35%)

⇒ (10,000 × 35/100)

⇒ Rs. 3,500

Selling price = Rs. (10,000 – 3,500)

⇒ Rs. 6,500

∴ Required selling price is Rs. 6,500

questions.question: An item costs Rs. 400. During a festival sale, a company offers a sale discount that offers x% off on its regular price along with a discount coupon of 10%. The price of the item after using both the sale discount and the discount coupon, is Rs. 216. What is the value of x?
questions.questionHtml: An item costs Rs. 400. During a festival sale, a company offers a sale discount that offers x% off on its regular price along with a discount coupon of 10%. The price of the item after using both the sale discount and the discount coupon, is Rs. 216. What is the value of x?
questions.solution:
Given:

The cost price of an item = Rs. 400

The selling price of the item = Rs. 216

Sale discount = x%

Coupon discount = 10%

Formula used:

The successive discount of a% and b% = (a + b - ab/100)%

Discount% = (Discount/M.P.) × 100

Where, M.P. = Marked price

Calculation:

Here, Marked price = The cost price of an item = Rs. 400

(Because discount is given on this price.)

The discount = 400 - 216 = Rs. 184

The total discount = (184/400) × 100 = 46%

So, x + 10 - (10x/100) = 46

⇒ x + 10 - x/10 = 46

⇒ 9x/10 + 10 = 46

⇒ 9x/10 = 46 - 10

⇒ 9x/10 = 36

⇒ x = 36 × (10/9) = 40

∴ The value of x is 40

questions.question: The difference between the selling prices obtained after a single discount of 45% and two successive discounts of 30% and 15% on the marked price Rs. 12,000 of an article is:
questions.questionHtml: The difference between the selling prices obtained after a single discount of 45% and two successive discounts of 30% and 15% on the marked price Rs. 12,000 of an article is:
questions.solution:
Given:

MP = Rs. 12,000

Case I: Discount = 45%

Case II: Successive Discount = 30% and 15%

Formula Used:

SP = MP - Discount

Calculation:

MP = 12,000

Case I: When discount = 45%

∴ SP = (100 - 45) % of 12,000

⇒ SP = 55% of 12,000

⇒ SP = 6,600

Case II: When successive discount = 30% and 15%

∴ SP = 70% of 85% of MP

⇒ SP = 70% of 85% of 12,000

⇒ SP = 7 × 85 × 12

⇒ SP = 7,140

∴, the difference between SPs = (7,140 - 6,600) = Rs. 540

questions.question: One dozen notebooks quoted at Rs. 125 are available at 20% discount. How many notebooks can be bought for Rs. 75?
questions.questionHtml: One dozen notebooks quoted at Rs. 125 are available at 20% discount. How many notebooks can be bought for Rs. 75?
questions.solution:

Discount % = 20%

Calculation:

Marked price of 12 notebooks = Rs.125

Selling price of 12 notebooks = 125 × 80/100 = Rs.100

Selling price of a notebook = 100/12 = Rs.25/3

∴ Number of notebooks bought for Rs.75 = 75 × 3/25 = 9

questions.question: A shopkeeper sells a table at a discount of 20 percent and earns a profit of 30 percent. If he sells the same table at 10 percent discount, then what will be his new profit or loss percent?
questions.questionHtml: A shopkeeper sells a table at a discount of 20 percent and earns a profit of 30 percent. If he sells the same table at 10 percent discount, then what will be his new profit or loss percent?
questions.solution:
After a 20% discount, the selling price is 80% of 100 = 80

This is also the cost price with 30% profit, so 80 = 1.3 × (Cost Price) ⇒ Cost Price = 80/1.3

Profit = Selling Price - Cost Price = 90 - (80/1.3) = (117 - 80) = 37/1.3 ⇒ 46.25%

questions.question: A dealer allows a 25% discount on the marked price of an article and gains 20%. If the cost price of the article increases by 20%, how much discount percentage should he allow on the marked price so as to earn the same percentage of profit as before?
questions.questionHtml: A dealer allows a 25% discount on the marked price of an article and gains 20%. If the cost price of the article increases by 20%, how much discount percentage should he allow on the marked price so as to earn the same percentage of profit as before?
questions.solution:
Calculation:

Let MP of the article be Rs. 100

SP of the article = 100 × (75/100)

⇒ Rs. 75 

According to the question profit is 20%

⇒ 120% of C.P = 75

⇒ CP of the article = 75 × (100/120)

Again According to the question

New CP = 75 × (100/120) × (120/100)

⇒ Rs. 75

⇒ New SP = 75 × (120/100)

⇒ Rs. 90

Discount percentage = [(100 – 90) /100] × 100

⇒ 10% 

∴ The required discount percent is 10%.

questions.question: A 25% profit is made when a discount of 25% is given on the marked price of an item. When the discount is 35%, what will be the profit? (Give your answer correct to the nearest whole number.)
questions.questionHtml: A 25% profit is made when a discount of 25% is given on the marked price of an item. When the discount is 35%, what will be the profit? (Give your answer correct to the nearest whole number.)
questions.solution:
Selling price = 100 + 25% of 100 = 125 Rs.

S.P = M. P – Discount = M.P – 25 % of M.P ⇒ 125 = M.P – \(\frac {25}{100}\) × M.P ⇒ M.P = Rs. \(\frac{500}{3}\)

New S.P = M.P – 35 % of M.P ⇒ New S.P =  \(\frac{500} {3} -\) \(\frac {35}{100} × \frac {500}{3}=\) Rs. \(\frac{325}{3}\) 

Profit % = \(\frac{325}{3}-100=\frac{325-300}{3}=\frac{25}{3}\) = 8 \(\frac{1}{3}\) ≈ 8 %

questions.question: A shopkeeper allows a 28% discount on the marked price of an article and still makes a profit of 20%. If he gains ₹30.80 on the sale of one article, then what is the selling price (in ₹) of the article?
questions.questionHtml: A shopkeeper allows a 28% discount on the marked price of an article and still makes a profit of 20%. If he gains ₹30.80 on the sale of one article, then what is the selling price (in ₹) of the article?
questions.solution:
Let the Marked price be Rs. 100

He gives 28% discount, ⇒ SP = 100 × (100 - 28)% = 100 × 72% = 72

He gains 20% on 72, then CP = 72 × 100/120 = 72 × 5/6 = 60

⇒ (72 - 60) = 12 unit → 30.80, now SP = 72 unit →  (30.80/12 × 72) = 184.80

questions.question: The marked price of 42 items was equal to the cost price of 70 items. The selling price of 25 items was equal to the marked price of 21 items. Calculate the percentage profit or loss from the sale of each item.
questions.questionHtml: The marked price of 42 items was equal to the cost price of 70 items. The selling price of 25 items was equal to the marked price of 21 items. Calculate the percentage profit or loss from the sale of each item.
questions.solution:
Let the marked price is M, selling price as S, cost price as C

⇒ \(42\times M=70\times C \) ⇒ \(\frac{M}{C}=\frac{70}{42}=\frac{10}{6}\) 

⇒ \(25\times S=21 \times M\) ⇒ \(\frac{S}{M}=\frac{21}{25}\)

Solving this we get ratio C : S : M :: 30 : 42 : 50

Profit % = \(\frac{S-C}{C}\times100\) = \(\frac{42-30}{30}\times100\) = 40%

questions.question: The marked price of a washing machine is Rs. 7,200 If it is sold for Rs. 5,512.50, after two successive discounts of x% each. The value of x is:
questions.questionHtml: The marked price of a washing machine is Rs. 7,200 If it is sold for Rs. 5,512.50, after two successive discounts of x% each. The value of x is:
questions.solution:
Given:

MP of the washing machine = Rs. 7200

SP of the washing machine = Rs. 5512.50

Concept used:

S.P = [(100 - D%)/100] × M.P

Discount = M.P - S.P

Calculation:

We know that,

S.P = [(100 - D%)/100] × M.P

⇒ 5512.50 = 7200 × [(100 - x)/100] × [(100 - x)/100]

⇒ [(100 - x)/100]2 = 5512.50/7200

⇒ [(100 - x)/100]2 = 49/64

⇒ [(100 - x)/100] = (49/64)1/2

⇒ [(100 - x)/100] = 7/8

⇒ 800 - 8x = 700

⇒ x = 100/8

⇒ x = 12.5

∴ The Required Percentage is 12.5%.


Shortcut Trick

12.5% = 1/8

64 unit = 7200

1 unit = 112.5

49 unit = 5512.5

questions.question: A discount of 20% is given on the marked price of a cycle, and still there is a profit of 20%. If the profit is Rs. 800, find the marked price of the cycle.
questions.questionHtml: A discount of 20% is given on the marked price of a cycle, and still there is a profit of 20%. If the profit is Rs. 800, find the marked price of the cycle.
questions.solution:
Given:

Discount (D) % = 20

Profit (P) % = 20

Profit = Rs. 800

Formula used:

Cost price (CP) / Marked price (MP) = (100 - D%) / (100 + P%)

Selling Price (SP) = MP × (100 - D%) / 100

Profit (P) = SP - CP

Calculation:

⇒ CP / MP = 80 / 120 ratio

⇒ SP = (120 × 80) / 100 = 96 ratio

⇒ P = 96 - 80

⇒ 800 = 16 ratio

⇒ 50 = 1 ratio

Now,

⇒ MP = 120 ratio = 120 × 50 = 6000

∴ The correct answer is 6000.

questions.question: A merchant announces 25% discount on the price of a shirt. If one needs to have a total rebate of Rs. 875 and the price of each shirt is Rs. 250. then how many shirts should the person purchase?
questions.questionHtml: A merchant announces 25% discount on the price of a shirt. If one needs to have a total rebate of Rs. 875 and the price of each shirt is Rs. 250. then how many shirts should the person purchase?
questions.solution:
Given:

The merchant gives a discount of 25% on each shirt having cost price of Rs 250

Calculations:

Discount of each shirt = 25% of 250 = 62.5 rupees

He wants a total of 875 rupees as a discount.

So,

Number of shirts he purchased × discount on each shirt = Total discount

Number of shirts × 62.5 = 875

The number of shirts = 875/62.5 = 14

∴ The correct choice will be option 3.

questions.question: A shopkeeper marks an article at such a price that after giving a discount of \(12\frac{1}{2}\) % on the marked price, he still earns a profit of 15%. What is the ratio of the marked price to the selling price of the article?
questions.questionHtml: A shopkeeper marks an article at such a price that after giving a discount of \(12\frac{1}{2}\) % on the marked price, he still earns a profit of 15%. What is the ratio of the marked price to the selling price of the article?
questions.solution:
Given:

Discount % = \(12\frac{1}{2}\)%

Profit % = 15%

Concept used:

Selling price = MP - MP × discount%

Calculation:

Let the marked price of the article be Rs. 8a

So, selling price = 8a - 8a × \(12\frac{1}{2}\)%

⇒ 7a

So, ratio = 8a : 7a

⇒ 8 : 7

∴ The ratio of the marked price to the selling price of the article is 8 : 7.

Additional InformationHere we do not need to calculate the cost price of the product

As in the question we have asked the ratio of Marked price and selling price

questions.question: Shopkeeper A marks up his price for an item at 25% and offers a discount of 15%. The same item is marked at 20% by another shopkeeper B and sold at a discount of 12%. Who gets a better deal in terms of % profit and by what profit percentage he sells that item?
questions.questionHtml: Shopkeeper A marks up his price for an item at 25% and offers a discount of 15%. The same item is marked at 20% by another shopkeeper B and sold at a discount of 12%. Who gets a better deal in terms of % profit and by what profit percentage he sells that item?
questions.solution:
Given:

Shopkeeper A:

Markup = 25%

Discount = 15%

Shopkeeper B:

Markup = 20%

Discount = 12%

Formula Used:

Effective Selling Price = Marked Price × (1 - Discount)

Profit Percentage = [(Selling Price - Cost Price) / Cost Price] × 100

Calculation:

Let the Cost Price (CP) of the item be ₹100 for simplicity.

Shopkeeper A:

Marked Price (MP) = CP × (1 + Markup)

MP = 100 × (1 + 0.25)

MP = 125

Selling Price = MP × (1 - Discount)

Selling Price = 125 × (1 - 0.15)

Selling Price = 125 × 0.85

Selling Price = 106.25

Profit = Selling Price - CP

Profit = 106.25 - 100

Profit = 6.25

Profit Percentage = (6.25 / 100) × 100

Profit Percentage = 6.25%

Shopkeeper B:

Marked Price (MP) = CP × (1 + Markup)

MP = 100 × (1 + 0.20)

MP = 120

Selling Price = MP × (1 - Discount)

Selling Price = 120 × (1 - 0.12)

Selling Price = 120 × 0.88

Selling Price = 105.6

Profit = Selling Price - CP

Profit = 105.6 - 100

Profit = 5.6

Profit Percentage = (5.6 / 100) × 100

Profit Percentage = 5.6%

Comparison:

Shopkeeper A has a profit percentage of 6.25%.

Shopkeeper B has a profit percentage of 5.6%.

Shopkeeper A gets a better deal with a profit percentage of 6.25%, compared to Shopkeeper B's profit percentage of 5.6%.

questions.question: A retailer buys 50 pens at the marked price of 44 pens. If he sells these pens at a discount of 1% on the marked price, what is the profit per cent?
questions.questionHtml: A retailer buys 50 pens at the marked price of 44 pens. If he sells these pens at a discount of 1% on the marked price, what is the profit per cent?
questions.solution:
Let the Market price 50 pens are 50

After getting 1 % discount the price should be 50 - 0.5 = 49.5

Now the cost Price will be market price of 44 pens that is Rs 44

So the profit will be 49.5 - 44 = 5.5

The profit percentage will be, ⇒(5.5 /44) × 100 = 12.5 %

questions.question: A person marks his goods x% above the cost price and allows a discount of 12% on the marked price. If his profit is 10%, then the difference between x% and the profit percentage is:
questions.questionHtml: A person marks his goods x% above the cost price and allows a discount of 12% on the marked price. If his profit is 10%, then the difference between x% and the profit percentage is:
questions.solution:
SP = 11/10 × CP

MP = {(100 + x)/100} × CP

SP = 88% of MP

⇒ SP = 88/100 × {(100 + x)/100} × CP

⇒ (110/100) × CP = 88/100 × {(100 + x)/100} × CP ⇒ 110 = 88 × (100 + x)/100 ⇒ 125 = 100 + x ⇒ x = 25.

The difference between x% and the profit percentage = 25 - 10 ⇒ 15%

questions.question: In a showroom the price of a washing machine is ₹65,000. The customer gets cash discount of ₹2,000, and gets a scratch card promising percentage discount of 10% to 15%. Determine the difference between the least and the maximum selling prices of the washing machine.

questions.question: A shopkeeper makes a net profit of 44% on selling an article at successive discounts of 10% and 20%. Find the net profit percentage, if the shopkeeper sells the same article at a discount of 15%.
questions.questionHtml: A shopkeeper makes a net profit of 44% on selling an article at successive discounts of 10% and 20%. Find the net profit percentage, if the shopkeeper sells the same article at a discount of 15%.

questions.question: The marked price of a chair is 30 percent more than its cost price. If the chair is sold for Rs. 200 after a discount of Rs. 40, then what will be the profit percentage?

questions.solution:

MP = 200 + 40 = 240

CP × 130% = 240 ⇒ CP = 2400/13 = 184.6

Profit = Selling price - Cost price = 200 - 184.6 = 15.38 

Profit percentage = (15.38/184.62) × 100 = 8.34%

questions.question: The marked price of an article is ₹ 1,000. It is sold for ₹ 712.89 after three successive discounts on the marked price, one of 10% and two of x% each. what is the value of x?
questions.questionHtml: The marked price of an article is ₹ 1,000. It is sold for ₹ 712.89 after three successive discounts on the marked price, one of 10% and two of x% each. what is the value of x?
questions.solution:
Given:

Market price = ₹1000

SP = ₹712.89

Three successive discounts on the marked price = 10%, and two of x% each

Concept Used:

SP = (1 - d1/100) (1 - d2/100) (1 - d3/100) x MRP

Calculation:

SP = (1 - d1/100) (1 - d2/100) (1 - d3/100) x MRP

⇒ 712.89 = (1 - 10/100) (1 - x/100) (1 - x/100) x 1000

⇒ 712.89/1000 = 9/10 x (100 - x)/100 x (100 - x)/100

⇒ 71289 = 9(100 - x)2

⇒ x2 - 200x + 2079 = 0

After solving above eq we get, 

x = 11

Therefore, the value of x is 11

questions.question: The marked price of a mobile phone was ₹35,600. The shop owner offered a 10% trade discount on the marked price but on further request by the customer, he sold the phone for ₹30,000 after giving a cash discount. How much is this cash discount as a percentage of the price after the trade discount? (Give your answer correct to 2 decimal places.)
questions.questionHtml: The marked price of a mobile phone was ₹35,600. The shop owner offered a 10% trade discount on the marked price but on further request by the customer, he sold the phone for ₹30,000 after giving a cash discount. How much is this cash discount as a percentage of the price after the trade discount? (Give your answer correct to 2 decimal places.)
questions.solution:
Given:- 

Selling price = Rs.35,000  

Trade discount = 10%, Final selling price = 30,000

Formula used:- 

Discount = \(\frac{Marked\ price - Selling\ price}{Marked\ price}\) 

Calculation:- 

The Selling price after a 10% trade discount will be-

SP = Marked Price - (discount %) × Marked Price

SP = 35,600 - (10% × 35,600)

⇒ SP = Rs. 32,040

The phone was sold at Rs. 30,000 

.·. Cash Discount = \(\frac{Selling\ Price- Price\ at\ Sold}{Selling\ Price}\)

⇒ \(\frac{32,040-30,000}{32,040}\) = \(\frac{2,040}{32,040}\)

⇒ 0.0636

Percent Cash Discount = 100 × 0.06367

⇒ Percent Cash Discount = 6.367%

On rounding off, The Percent Cash Discount = 6.37%

The percent cash discount given after 10% trade discount is 6.37%.

questions.question: A trader sells an item for Rs. 516.60 after offering a discount of 18% on its list price. Had he not given the discount, he would have earned a profit of 26%. What is the cost price (in Rs.) of the item?
questions.questionHtml: A trader sells an item for Rs. 516.60 after offering a discount of 18% on its list price. Had he not given the discount, he would have earned a profit of 26%. What is the cost price (in Rs.) of the item?
questions.solution:
Formula used:

CP = MP × \(100\over(100+G)\), where

CP = Cost Price

MP = Marked Price

G = Gain%

Calculation:

Let the marked price be Rs 100

Selling price after 18% discount = Rs 100 - Rs 18 = Rs 82

⇒ x = Rs 516.60 × \(100\over82\) = Rs 630

Cost Price = Rs 630 × \(100\over126\) = Rs 500

∴ The cost price is Rs 500.

questions.question: An article was marked at Rs. x and sold at a discount of (x - 40)%. If the customer paid Rs. (x - 32), then find the marked priced of the article
questions.questionHtml: An article was marked at Rs. x and sold at a discount of (x - 40)%. If the customer paid Rs. (x - 32), then find the marked priced of the article
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Test the options to find the Marked Price (x) that satisfies the given conditions.

For x = 80: Discount % = (80 − 40)% = 40%.

Discount Value = 40% of 80 = (40/100) × 80 = Rs. 32.

Selling Price (SP) = Marked Price − Discount = 80 − 32 = Rs. 48.

Check SP condition: SP = x − 32 = 80 − 32 = Rs. 48. (Condition satisfied)

∴ The correct answer is Rs. 80.

Alternate Method

Given:

Marked Price (MP) = Rs. x

Discount Percentage = (x − 40)%

Selling Price (SP) = Rs. (x − 32)

Formula Used:

SP = MP × (100 − Discount %)/100

Calculations:

⇒ (x − 32) = x × [100 − (x − 40)] / 100

⇒ 100 × (x − 32) = x × (100 − x + 40)

⇒ 100x − 3200 = x × (140 − x)

⇒ 100x − 3200 = 140x − x2

⇒ x2 − 40x − 3200 = 0

⇒ x2 − 80x + 40x − 3200 = 0

⇒ x(x − 80) + 40(x − 80) = 0

⇒ (x − 80)(x + 40) = 0

⇒ x = 80 or x = −40

⇒ Since price cannot be negative, x = 80.

∴ The correct answer is Rs. 80.

Additional Information

Relationship between SP and MP

The Selling Price is obtained by subtracting the Discount amount from the Marked Price: SP = MP − Discount.

Discount Percentage Formula

The Discount Percentage is calculated on the Marked Price: Discount % = (Discount / MP) × 100.

Quadratic Formula for Roots

For an equation ax2 + bx + c = 0, the roots are given by x = [−b ± √(b2 − 4ac)] / 2a.

questions.question: A renowned brand marked its goods at 40% above the cost price but allows a discount of 7.5% for UPI payments to the customers. What actual profit is made on a shirt, if a customer pays ₹1,813 to buy it using UPI?
questions.questionHtml: A renowned brand marked its goods at 40% above the cost price but allows a discount of 7.5% for UPI payments to the customers. What actual profit is made on a shirt, if a customer pays ₹1,813 to buy it using UPI?
questions.solution:
Given:

The marked price of the article is 40% above the cost price

Discount of 7.5% on UPI payments

Concept Used:

Marked price (MP) = 100 × SP/(100 - d)

Where SP = Selling price, and d = discount percentage

Calculation:

Selling Price of the shirt = Rs. 1813

According to the formula,

Marked price (MP) of the shirt

⇒ 100 × 1813 / (100 - 7.5) = Rs. 1960

Now the MP of the shirt is 40% more than the cost price (CP)

So, CP = 100 × 1960 / (100 + 40) = Rs. 1400

Profit earned = (1813 - 1400) = Rs. 413

∴ Actual profit made on the shirt is Rs. 413
